:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.3`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noBooleanSortComparator`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**error**](/reference/diagnostics#error).
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`unicorn/no-boolean-sort-comparator`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/main/docs/rules/no-boolean-sort-comparator.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noBooleanSortComparator": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow sort comparators that return a boolean.

`Array#sort()` and `Array#toSorted()` accept a comparator: a function that receives two items and returns a number.
A negative number puts the first item before the second, a positive number puts it after, and zero keeps their current order.

When a comparator returns `true` or `false`, the sort method treats `true` as `1` and `false` as `0`.
The comparator can then never say that the first item comes first, so the items aren't sorted correctly,
and the result can differ between browsers and JavaScript runtimes.

Return a number instead: subtract numbers from each other, or use `String#localeCompare()` for strings.

This rule checks comparators whose body is a single expression or a single `return` statement,
comparators with a `boolean` return type, and references to functions that return a boolean,
such as `Boolean` or `Number.isNaN`. It doesn't check comparators that contain several `return` statements.

## Examples

### Invalid

```js
array.sort((a, b) => a > b);
```

The items aren't sorted correctly, and the result can differ between JavaScript engines.</span><br />  <br />  <strong><span style=\"color: lightgreen;\">ℹ</span></strong> <span style=\"color: lightgreen;\">Return a negative number, zero, or a positive number instead, such as </span><span style=\"color: lightgreen;\"><strong>a - b</strong></span><span style=\"color: lightgreen;\"> for numbers or </span><span style=\"color: lightgreen;\"><strong>a.localeCompare(b)</strong></span><span style=\"color: lightgreen;\"> for strings.</span><br />  <br />  <strong><span style=\"color: lightgreen;\">ℹ</span></strong> <span style=\"color: lightgreen;\">This rule belongs to the nursery group, which means it is not yet stable and may change in the future. Visit </span><span style=\"color: lightgreen;\"><a href=\"https://biomejs.dev/linter/#nursery\">https://biomejs.dev/linter/#nursery</a></span><span style=\"color: lightgreen;\"> for more information.</span><br />  <br /></code></pre>"} />

### Valid

```js
array.sort((a, b) => a - b);
array.toSorted((a, b) => a.score - b.score);
strings.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b));
array.sort((a, b) => (a > b ? 1 : a < b ? -1 : 0));
```
